Michael R. Douglas and Cristofero Fraser-Taliente
Figure 1: Average solution length against number of nodes expanded, for
1000 initial states randomly scrambled between 1000-10000 times. We report
results with a ball radius R = 5, and no T-calibration. For beam width 27
or greater, we are able to solve all states.
Figure 2: Average solution length vs beam width. We find a best fit given
by E = 41.9log2(B)−1 −1.92, where B is the beam width (trivially related
to the number of nodes). Excesses are always even due to parity. We report
results with a ball radius R = 5, and no T-calibration.
